themes_detail.label: Elevator Crisis in Housing
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a sudden breakdown or maintenance failure affecting multiple residential buildings in Riverdale/Fieldston THIS WEEK.
evidence: 3 elevator complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Concentrated spike suggests systemic failure rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Contact Buildings Department to identify which buildings filed complaints and whether violations were issued; interview residents in affected buildings about disruption
Investigate whether this coincides with a city-wide elevator maintenance delay or contractor issue

themes_detail.label: Root and Sewer Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 4 last week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% spike (z-score: 5.67)—indicating accelerating underground infrastructure failure affecting multiple properties in the district LAST WEEK.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints filed last week vs. 0.2 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.67 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Aligns with CB budget request for park upgrades and maintenance, suggesting ongoing systemic neglect
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint addresses with DEP maintenance records; investigate whether aging sewer lines in Riverdale are approaching end-of-life
Interview property owners and residents about costs of root damage and remediation; determine if city is delaying repairs

themes_detail.label: Park Noise and Encampment Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK (z-score: 3.77) and encampment complaints peaked at 4 three weeks ago (z-score: 4.95, up 700%), suggesting concentrated homeless encampment activity and associated disturbances in district parks OVER THE PAST 3 WEEKS.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
4 encampment complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 average weekly complaints (700% increase)
CB budget request for park reconstruction/upgrades and maintenance equipment suggests parks are under-resourced
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are affected; visit sites to assess encampment size, conditions, and impact on community use
Interview Parks Department about sanitation and outreach response; speak with residents and park users about safety and access concerns

themes_detail.label: Residential Door and Window Damage Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Door/window complaints increased to 21 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 12.9 per week—a 63% spike (z-score: 3.51)—indicating a recent surge in break-ins, vandalism, or building maintenance failures affecting residential security THIS WEEK.
evidence: 21 door/window complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 12.9 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.51 represents statistically significant deviation
Spike timing suggests either concentrated break-in activity or weather/infrastructure event
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD to determine whether complaints correlate with reported burglaries or break-ins; check crime statistics for the district
Cross-reference with weather data to assess whether recent storms caused widespread damage; interview landlords about maintenance backlog

themes_detail.label: Street Signage Disappearance
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints tripled to 3 last week versus a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 243% spike (z-score: 3.54)—indicating accelerated theft, vandalism, or poor city maintenance of directional infrastructure LAST WEEK.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints filed last week vs. 0.9 average weekly complaints over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.54 indicates statistically significant spike
CB budget request for traffic/pedestrian safety suggests ongoing DOT resource constraints
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DOT for sign replacement work orders in CD 208; determine replacement timeline
Investigate whether signs are being stolen for scrap metal or removed during construction; assess impact on wayfinding and traffic safety
